title: a job queue drained by three workers with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED

steps.sql:
BEGIN;
SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE done_by IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 2 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
steps.note: W1 opens a transaction and claims the two oldest jobs that nobody holds: 1 and 2. they're row-locked by W1 now.

steps.sql:
BEGIN;
SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE done_by IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 2 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
steps.note: W2 runs the exact same query. 1 and 2 are locked, so it skips them and gets 3 and 4. no waiting.

steps.sql:
BEGIN;
SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE done_by IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 2 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
UPDATE jobs SET done_by = 'W1' WHERE id IN (1, 2)
steps.note: W1 sends its two emails and marks them done.
W1 commits. jobs 1 and 2 are done, and their locks are gone.

steps.sql:
BEGIN;
SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE done_by IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 2 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
steps.note: W1 comes back for more. 1 and 2 are done, 3 to 6 are locked, so it gets the only one left: 7.

steps.sql:
UPDATE jobs SET done_by = 'W3' WHERE id IN (5, 6);
COMMIT

UPDATE jobs SET done_by = 'W2' WHERE id IN (3, 4);
COMMIT

UPDATE jobs SET done_by = 'W1' WHERE id = 7;
COMMIT
SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE done_by IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 2 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
steps.note: W2 asks again: nothing left. an empty result, and no waiting.

steps.sql: SELECT id, done_by FROM jobs ORDER BY id
steps.note: seven jobs, three workers, every job done exactly once.
